[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

Adopt Agile Manifesto principles and Scrum framework as the standard development methodology for all project teams, implementing DevOps practices with defined roles, ceremonies, and work item structures to enable efficient team collaboration and continuous delivery.

---
page_texts.5:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Gainwell technology teams need a consistent, scalable development methodology that enables rapid delivery of business value while maintaining quality standards. Teams must work collaboratively across multiple projects and products, requiring standardized processes and tools that support agile principles.
page_texts.6:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Development teams work on complex healthcare technology solutions with varying requirements, timelines, and stakeholder needs. Without standardized agile practices, teams experience inconsistent delivery patterns, communication gaps, and difficulty in managing dependencies across projects.
page_texts.7:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

How should project team members integrate and collaborate to accomplish tasks in an agile fashion that meets business requirements while maintaining quality, predictability, and team efficiency?
page_texts.8:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#decision-drivers]

### Decision Drivers

- 🎯 **Business Value Delivery**: Maximize value delivered through iterative development
- 🤝 **Team Collaboration**: Enable effective collaboration across distributed teams
- 📊 **Transparency**: Provide visibility into work progress and team capacity
- 🔄 **Continuous Improvement**: Foster culture of retrospection and improvement
- ⚡ **Speed to Market**: Accelerate delivery through agile practices
- 📈 **Predictability**: Improve estimation accuracy and delivery predictability
- 🏗️ **DevOps Integration**: Align development with DevOps principles

---
page_texts.10:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#agile-scrum-with-devops-practices]

### Agile Scrum with DevOps Practices

**Description**: Implement Scrum framework following Agile Manifesto principles with integrated DevOps practices including continuous integration, automated testing, and collaborative development patterns.

**Implementation Details**:
page_texts.12:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#project-manager]

##### Project Manager

- Manages scope, cost, quality, personnel, communication, risk, and procurement
- Ensures project governance and compliance requirements are met
- **Critical Success Factor**: Must resist translating Story Points to hours and avoid using daily standup as a status meeting
page_texts.13:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#product-owner]

##### Product Owner

- Represents business stakeholders and end users
- Maintains and prioritizes product backlog
- Ensures team delivers maximum value in correct order
- **Critical Success Factor**: Must be actively involved daily with backlog management, not just a figurehead
page_texts.14:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#scrum-master]

##### Scrum Master

- Facilitates Scrum ceremonies and removes impediments
- Ensures team follows Scrum practices effectively
- Coaches team on agile principles and continuous improvement
- **Critical Success Factor**: Must have technical understanding of project architecture to effectively communicate with team and remove blockers
page_texts.15:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#development-team]

##### Development Team

- Cross-functional skilled technicians who deliver working software
- Self-organizing and collaborative
- Responsible for estimation, design, and delivery
- **Critical Success Factor**: Must possess strong technical skills, willingness to pair-program, carefully review pull requests, and actively contribute to Scrum/Kanban Board
page_texts.17:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#epics]

##### Epics

- **Purpose**: Define major functional areas using Domain Driven Design (DDD) patterns
- **Ownership**: Product Owner, Project Manager, and Scrum Master collaborate
- **Scope**: Business milestones spanning multiple features across multiple sprints
- **Characteristics**: High-level business initiatives aligned to strategic objectives
page_texts.18:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#features]

##### Features

- **Purpose**: Describe complete functional capabilities within an Epic
- **Ownership**: Product Owner and Scrum Master collaborate
- **Implementation**: Feature branch created from release branch with Draft Pull Request
- **Characteristics**:
    - Contains multiple User Stories
    - Source of truth for business requirements
    - Persistent for project lifetime
    - Can be reactivated as new requirements emerge
page_texts.19:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#user-stories]

##### User Stories

- **Purpose**: Describe specific user-facing functionality
- **Ownership**: Product Owner, Scrum Master, and Development Team collaborate
- **Requirements**: Must include minimum of Coding and Reviewing tasks
- **Implementation**: Individual branch derived from main branch with corresponding Pull Request
- **Format**: "As a [user type], I want [goal] so that [benefit]"
page_texts.20:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#tasks]

##### Tasks

- **Purpose**: Break down User Stories into actionable work items
- **Ownership**: Development Team defines and manages
- **Tracking**: Developers track time against tasks for completed hours during sprint
page_texts.22:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#backlog-grooming]

##### Backlog Grooming

- **Purpose**: Refine and estimate upcoming work items
- **Frequency**: Regular sessions throughout sprint
- **Participants**: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team
page_texts.23:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#sprint-planning]

##### Sprint Planning

- **Purpose**: Define sprint goals and commit to deliverables
- **Frequency**: Beginning of each sprint
- **Participants**: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team
page_texts.24:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#daily-scrum-standup]

##### Daily Scrum (Standup)

- **Purpose**: Synchronize team activities and identify blockers
- **Frequency**: Daily, time-boxed to 15 minutes
- **Participants**: Development Team, Scrum Master (facilitator)
- **Format**: What did I complete? What am I working on? What blockers do I have?
page_texts.25:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#sprint-review]

##### Sprint Review

- **Purpose**: Demonstrate completed work to stakeholders
- **Frequency**: End of each sprint
- **Participants**: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Development Team, Stakeholders
page_texts.26:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#sprint-retrospective]

##### Sprint Retrospective

- **Purpose**: Reflect on sprint process and identify improvements
- **Frequency**: End of each sprint, after Sprint Review
- **Participants**: Scrum Master, Development Team
page_texts.27:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#devops-integration]

#### DevOps Integration

The project adopts DevOps philosophy incorporating:

- **Continuous Integration**: Automated build and test on every commit
- **Continuous Deployment**: Automated deployment to non-production environments
- **Infrastructure as Code**: All infrastructure defined in version control
- **Monitoring and Logging**: Comprehensive observability of applications
- **Collaboration**: Breaking down silos between development and operations
- **Automation**: Maximizing automation across the delivery pipeline
- **Measurement**: Data-driven decision making through metrics
- **Sharing**: Knowledge sharing and collective ownership
page_texts.29:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#branch-naming-convention]

##### Branch Naming Convention

- User Story branches: `us####` (where #### is the user story number)
- Feature branches: Named descriptively for the feature
- Branches deleted once completed or aborted
page_texts.30:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#pull-request-process]

##### Pull Request Process

1. Contributors pull latest code from main branch regularly to avoid conflicts
2. All Feature Scenarios must run successfully
3. Code must meet Definition of Done
4. Contributors vote to complete Pull Request
5. Automated notifications to subscribers
6. Contributors manage their own subscriptions
7. SME review requested when necessary

**Pros**:

- ✅ **Proven Framework**: Scrum is well-established with extensive community support
- ✅ **Iterative Delivery**: Regular delivery of working software every sprint
- ✅ **Team Empowerment**: Self-organizing teams with clear accountability
- ✅ **Transparency**: Regular ceremonies provide visibility into progress
- ✅ **Adaptability**: Retrospectives enable continuous process improvement
- ✅ **Risk Mitigation**: Early and frequent delivery reduces project risk
- ✅ **Stakeholder Engagement**: Regular reviews keep stakeholders informed and involved
- ✅ **DevOps Alignment**: Integrates seamlessly with DevOps practices

**Cons**:

- ❌ **Learning Curve**: Teams new to Scrum require training and coaching
- ❌ **Discipline Required**: Success depends on team commitment to practices
- ❌ **Time Investment**: Ceremonies require dedicated time from team members
- ❌ **Role Clarity**: Requires clear understanding and adherence to Scrum roles
- ❌ **Cultural Change**: May require significant organizational culture shift

---
page_texts.32:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#option-1-waterfall-development]

### Option 1: Waterfall Development

**Description**: Traditional sequential development with distinct phases (requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment)

**Pros**:

- ✅ Familiar to traditional project managers
- ✅ Clear phase gates and documentation
- ✅ Predictable timelines for simple projects

**Cons**:

- ❌ Inflexible to changing requirements
- ❌ Late discovery of issues
- ❌ Limited stakeholder feedback until late stages
- ❌ High risk for complex projects
- ❌ Does not align with DevOps principles
page_texts.33:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#option-2-kanban-only]

### Option 2: Kanban Only

**Description**: Continuous flow methodology without fixed sprints or roles

**Pros**:

- ✅ Flexible work in progress limits
- ✅ No fixed sprint commitments
- ✅ Simpler to implement

**Cons**:

- ❌ Less structured planning and retrospection
- ❌ No defined roles like Scrum Master or Product Owner
- ❌ Can lack accountability without sprint commitments
- ❌ Difficult to predict delivery timelines
page_texts.34:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#option-3-hybrid-scrum-kanban-scrumban]

### Option 3: Hybrid Scrum-Kanban (Scrumban)

**Description**: Combines Scrum's structured approach with Kanban's flow management

**Pros**:

- ✅ Flexibility of Kanban with structure of Scrum
- ✅ Suitable for support and development mix

**Cons**:

- ❌ Can be confusing without clear guidelines
- ❌ Less standardized than pure Scrum
- ❌ May dilute benefits of both methodologies

---
page_texts.35:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#decision-outcome]

## Decision Outcome

**Chosen Option**: Agile Scrum with DevOps Practices (see Recommended Option above)
page_texts.36:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#rationale]

### Rationale

- Provides proven framework with clear roles and ceremonies
- Enables iterative delivery with regular stakeholder feedback
- Supports continuous improvement through retrospectives
- Aligns with DevOps principles and modern development practices
- Provides transparency and predictability through defined sprints
- Industry standard with extensive tooling and community support
- Facilitates collaboration through structured ceremonies
- Enables scaling across multiple teams with consistent practices
page_texts.38:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#tooling-requirements]

#### Tooling Requirements

Teams must use tools supporting:

- Backlog management and work item tracking
- Sprint planning and burndown tracking
- Branch and pull request management
- Automated build and test execution
- Collaboration and communication

Reference the Agile Team Development section of Adopted Software Technologies for specific tool selections.
page_texts.39:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#definition-of-done]

#### Definition of Done

All User Stories must meet the following criteria before being marked complete:

- Code complete and reviewed
- Unit tests written and passing
- Integration tests passing
- Documentation updated
- Code merged to main branch
- Deployed to development environment
- Acceptance criteria met and verified by Product Owner
page_texts.40:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#work-breakdown-structure]

#### Work Breakdown Structure

Use deliverable-based Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) to organize project work hierarchically:

- Level 1: Project
- Level 2: Epics (major deliverables)
- Level 3: Features (functional capabilities)
- Level 4: User Stories (user-facing functionality)
- Level 5: Tasks (implementation work)

---
page_texts.42:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#positive]

### Positive

- ✅ Consistent development process across all teams
- ✅ Improved team collaboration and communication
- ✅ Regular delivery of working software
- ✅ Early identification and resolution of issues
- ✅ Better alignment with business priorities
- ✅ Increased transparency and predictability
- ✅ Continuous improvement through retrospectives
- ✅ Enhanced team morale through empowerment
- ✅ Facilitates pair programming and code reviews
- ✅ Supports DevOps practices and automation
page_texts.43:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#negative]

### Negative

- ❌ Requires discipline and commitment from all team members
- ❌ Initial learning curve for teams new to Scrum
- ❌ Ceremony time overhead (typically 10-15% of sprint capacity)
- ❌ Requires active Product Owner participation
- ❌ May be challenging to estimate complex work initially
page_texts.44:
[decisions/governance/ADR-GOV-003-agile-team-development.md#neutral]

### Neutral

- 🔄 Requires investment in team training and coaching
- 🔄 May need organizational culture shift
- 🔄 Metrics interpretation requires experience
- 🔄 Tool selection and configuration needed
